```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

# --------------------------------------------------
# Example: one ZIP code's monthly totals
# --------------------------------------------------
# Replace this with your actual data
monthly = pd.DataFrame({
    "month": np.arange(1, 13),
    "total": [
        120, 110, 105, 100, 115, 140,
        165, 180, 175, 155, 140, 130
    ]
})

monthly = pd.read_csv('../project-workbook-hayden_logan_m/shared_data/monthly_solar.csv')

```

```{python}
monthly
```

```{python}

# Month as 0-11 for the Fourier representation
t = monthly["month"].values - 1

# --------------------------------------------------
# Fit one annual sine wave
# --------------------------------------------------
X = np.column_stack([
    np.ones(len(t)),
    np.cos(2 * np.pi * t / 12),
    np.sin(2 * np.pi * t / 12)
])

model = LinearRegression(fit_intercept=False)
model.fit(X, monthly["total"])

beta0, beta_cos, beta_sin = model.coef_

# Fitted values
monthly["fit"] = model.predict(X)

# --------------------------------------------------
# Convert coefficients into interpretable features
# --------------------------------------------------
amplitude = np.sqrt(beta_cos**2 + beta_sin**2)

# Phase / location of peak
phase = np.arctan2(beta_sin, beta_cos)

# Month corresponding approximately to peak
peak_month = (phase * 12 / (2 * np.pi)) % 12
peak_month = peak_month + 1

# R²
r2 = model.score(X, monthly["total"])

print("Fourier features")
print("----------------")
print(f"Baseline:     {beta0:.2f}")
print(f"Cosine:       {beta_cos:.2f}")
print(f"Sine:         {beta_sin:.2f}")
print(f"Amplitude:    {amplitude:.2f}")
print(f"Peak month:   {peak_month:.2f}")
print(f"R²:           {r2:.3f}")

# --------------------------------------------------
# Plot
# --------------------------------------------------
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))

plt.plot(
    monthly["month"],
    monthly["total"],
    marker="o",
    label="Actual monthly totals"
)

plt.plot(
    monthly["month"],
    monthly["fit"],
    marker="o",
    linestyle="--",
    label="Fitted seasonal wave"
)

plt.xticks(range(1, 13))
plt.xlabel("Month")
plt.ylabel("Total")
plt.title("Monthly Seasonality and Fourier Fit")
plt.legend()
plt.grid(alpha=0.25)

plt.show()
```

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

# --------------------------------------------------
# Select one ZIP code
# --------------------------------------------------
zip_data = monthly.loc[monthly["Zip Code"] == 97201].iloc[0]

# Monthly columns in calendar order
months = ["jan", "feb", "mar", "apr", "may", "jun",
          "jul", "aug", "sep", "oct", "nov", "dec"]

values = np.array([
    zip_data[f"solrad_{month}"] for month in months
], dtype=float)

# --------------------------------------------------
# Fit one annual Fourier/sine wave
# --------------------------------------------------
t = np.arange(12)

X = np.column_stack([
    np.ones(12),
    np.cos(2 * np.pi * t / 12),
    np.sin(2 * np.pi * t / 12)
])

model = LinearRegression(fit_intercept=False)
model.fit(X, values)

beta0, beta_cos, beta_sin = model.coef_

# --------------------------------------------------
# Smooth fitted curve
# --------------------------------------------------
t_smooth = np.linspace(0, 12, 300)

y_smooth = (
    beta0
    + beta_cos * np.cos(2 * np.pi * t_smooth / 12)
    + beta_sin * np.sin(2 * np.pi * t_smooth / 12)
)

# --------------------------------------------------
# Fourier features
# --------------------------------------------------
amplitude = np.sqrt(beta_cos**2 + beta_sin**2)
phase = np.arctan2(beta_sin, beta_cos)

r2 = model.score(X, values)

print(f"ZIP Code: 97003")
print()
print("Fourier features")
print("----------------")
print(f"Baseline (β₀):  {beta0:.4f}")
print(f"Cosine (βc):    {beta_cos:.4f}")
print(f"Sine (βs):       {beta_sin:.4f}")
print(f"Amplitude:       {amplitude:.4f}")
print(f"Phase:            {phase:.4f}")
print(f"R²:               {r2:.4f}")

# --------------------------------------------------
# Plot
# --------------------------------------------------
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))

# Actual monthly values
ax.bar(
    months,
    values,
    alpha=0.6,
    label="Actual monthly totals"
)

# Smooth Fourier fit
ax.plot(
    t_smooth / 12 * 12,  # keep x-axis in month positions
    y_smooth,
    linewidth=2.5,
    label="Fitted seasonal wave"
)

ax.set_xticks(t)
ax.set_xticklabels(months)

#ax.set_xlabel("Month")
ax.set_ylabel("Solar radiation (kWh/m²/day)")
ax.set_title("Portland, OR (97201) — Monthly Seasonality")
ax.legend()

feature_text = (
    f"Baseline = {baseline:.2f}\n"
    f"Amplitude = {amplitude:.2f}\n"
    f"Phase = {phase:.2f}\n"
    f"R² = {r2:.3f}"
)

ax.text(
    0.02, 0.97,
    feature_text,
    transform=ax.transAxes,
    verticalalignment="top",
    bbox=dict(boxstyle="round", facecolor="white", alpha=0.8)
)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```


```{python}
# --------------------------------------------------
# Convert Fourier coefficients to
# baseline, amplitude, and phase
# --------------------------------------------------
baseline = beta0

amplitude = np.sqrt(beta_cos**2 + beta_sin**2)

phase = np.arctan2(beta_cos, beta_sin)

# --------------------------------------------------
# Smooth fitted sine wave
# --------------------------------------------------
t_smooth = np.linspace(0, 12, 300)

y_smooth = (
    baseline
    + amplitude * np.sin(
        2 * np.pi * t_smooth / 12 + phase
    )
)

# --------------------------------------------------
# Features
# --------------------------------------------------
r2 = model.score(X, values)

print(f"ZIP Code: 97003")
print()
print("Seasonality features")
print("--------------------")
print(f"Baseline:   {baseline:.4f}")
print(f"Amplitude:  {amplitude:.4f}")
print(f"Phase:      {phase:.4f} radians")
print(f"R²:         {r2:.4f}")
```
